title: Unsupervised Learning — Move the Group Centers

body:
## Move the Group Centers

Dots on a map seem to form neighborhoods, but nobody marked the borders. Start with a few centers and repeatedly assign each dot to its nearest center.

That procedure is K-means clustering. After assignment, each center moves to the average position of its group, and the cycle repeats.

Scaling matters because a large-numbered feature can dominate distance. The chosen number of groups also changes the story you find.
common_mistakes: Calling clusters true labels without inspecting them.
Using distance before putting features on comparable scales.
Choosing the number of groups only because one chart looks attractive.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Move the Group Centers” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Many datasets have no labels, yet their groups, unusual cases, and compressed structure are valuable.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Move the Group Centers” story, explain Unsupervised Learning without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
